record.context_brief: The Bartoszyński-Tsaban set H and S1(Γ,Γ)
record.original_question: Let Z be the Cantor-like space of nondecreasing functions f in N^(N ∪ {∞}) such that whenever f(n) < ∞ one has f(n) < f(n+1), let Q be the dense set of eventually-∞ sequences q_s coming from increasing finite sequences s, let B = {f_α : α < b} be a <=*-unbounded b-scale of strictly increasing functions in N^N, and let H = B ∪ Q. Must H satisfy S_1(Γ, Γ), that is, for every sequence of open γ-covers of H can one choose one element from each cover so that the chosen family is again a γ-cover of H?

evidence.quote: Let B = {fα : α < b} ⊆ NN be a ≤∗-unbounded set of strictly increasing elements of NN which forms a b-scale (that is, for each α < β, fα ≤∗ fβ), and set H = B ∪ Q. In [6] it is proved that all finite powers of H satisfy Ufin(O, Γ). Problem 6.1 ([6, Problem 17], [57, Problem 2]). Does H satisfy S1(Γ, Γ)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and consider the space $Z$ of all nondecreasing functions $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$ such that whenever $f(n)<\infty$ one has $f(n)<f(n+1)$. Endow $Z$ with the subspace topology inherited from $(\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\})^{\mathbb{N}}$, where $\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$ is the one-point compactification of the discrete space $\mathbb{N}$; then $Z$ is a Cantor-like (compact metrizable, zero-dimensional) space. For each finite strictly increasing sequence $s=(s_0,\dots,s_{k-1})\in\mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$, define $q_s\in Z$ by $q_s(i)=s_i$ for $i<k$ and $q_s(i)=\infty$ for $i\geq k$; let $Q=\{q_s:s\text{ a finite strictly increasing sequence in }\mathbb{N}\}$, a countable dense subset of $Z$.

Let $\mathfrak{b}$ denote the bounding number, i.e., the minimal cardinality of a $\leq^*$-unbounded subset of $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, where $f\leq^* g$ means $f(n)\leq g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$. A $\mathfrak{b}$-scale is a family $\{f_\alpha:\alpha<\mathfrak{b}\}\subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ which is $\leq^*$-unbounded and satisfies $f_\alpha\leq^* f_\beta$ whenever $\alpha<\beta<\mathfrak{b}$. Fix such a scale $B=\{f_\alpha:\alpha<\mathfrak{b}\}$ consisting of strictly increasing functions in $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}\subseteq Z$, and set $H = B\cup Q\subseteq Z$.

An open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of a topological space $X$ is called a $\gamma$-cover if $\mathcal{U}$ is infinite and for every $x\in X$ the set $\{U\in\mathcal{U}: x\notin U\}$ is finite. The selection principle $S_1(\Gamma,\Gamma)$ states: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of open $\gamma$-covers of $X$ one may choose $U_n\in\mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{U_n:n\in\mathbb{N}\}$ is a $\gamma$-cover of $X$.

Question: Must the set $H$ defined above satisfy $S_1(\Gamma,\Gamma)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a known question of Bartoszyński and Tsaban (also listed as a problem of Tsaban). Subsequent work by Miller and Tsaban ("Point-cofinite covers in the Laver model", arXiv:0910.4063) establishes related consistency results about sets of size $\mathfrak{b}$ satisfying $S_1(\Gamma,\Gamma)$ (e.g., the existence of an unbounded tower implies there is a set of reals of cardinality $\mathfrak{b}$ satisfying $S_1(\Gamma,\Gamma)$, and consistently every such set has cardinality $<\mathfrak{b}$), but no source located confirms a definitive resolution of whether the specific set $H = B\cup Q$ must satisfy $S_1(\Gamma,\Gamma)$. The status appears to remain unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: Point-cofinite covers in the Laver model
status_evidence.snippet: If there is an unbounded tower, then there are sets of reals of cardinality b satisfying S_1(Gamma,Gamma). It is consistent that all sets of reals satisfying S_1(Gamma,Gamma) have cardinality smaller than b.
status_evidence.claim: Related consistency results about S_1(Gamma,Gamma) and cardinality b, but the specific question about H is not resolved.
